name: PCT2075 temperature sensor
description: NXP LM75-compatible digital temperature sensor and thermal watchdog, -55 to 125 °C with 0.125 °C resolution (±1 °C from -25 to 100 °C), on an I2C bus (up to 1 MHz), plus an open-drain over-temperature output. Runs on 2.7–5.5 V. Sold as: Adafruit PCT2075 Temperature Sensor - STEMMA QT / Qwiic (product 4369; 5-pin header VCC, GND, SCL, SDA, INT and a 3-pin header A0, A1, A2 on the opposite edge), I2C address 0x37 with A0/A1/A2 left floating (27 addresses possible).
eli5: A small thermometer chip your board asks for the temperature over two wires; it can also flip a pin when it gets too hot.

pins.name: VCC
pins.description: Supply, 2.7–5.5 V, no regulator (use the microcontroller's 3.3 V: the board's SDA/SCL pull-ups go to VCC)

pins.name: SCL
pins.description: I2C clock (10k pull-up to VCC on the board)

pins.name: SDA
pins.description: I2C data (10k pull-up to VCC on the board)

pins.name: INT
pins.description: OS over-temperature output, open-drain, active low by default; not needed for basic use

pins.name: A0
pins.description: Address bit 0 (other header): leave floating, tie to GND or VCC; sampled at power-up

pins.name: A1
pins.description: Address bit 1: leave floating, tie to GND or VCC; sampled at power-up

pins.name: A2
pins.description: Address bit 2: leave floating, tie to GND or VCC; sampled at power-up

supplierQuery: Adafruit PCT2075 temperature sensor STEMMA QT 4369
buildNotes: The board has two headers on opposite edges (VCC, GND, SCL, SDA, INT and A0, A1, A2), so wire it with jumper leads; only VCC, GND, SCL and SDA are needed.
With A0, A1 and A2 left floating (as shipped) the address is 0x37. Each pin can be floating, low or high, giving 27 addresses (datasheet Table 5); the pins are sampled only at power-up.
Temperature is register 0x00, two bytes MSB first: an 11-bit two's complement value in bits 15–5, 0.125 °C per step. Read both bytes; T = (signed 16-bit raw >> 5) × 0.125.
A conversion takes about 28 ms and repeats every 100 ms by default (Tidle register 0x04 sets 100 ms–3.1 s); the first reading is valid about 100 ms after power-up.
INT (OS) goes low when the temperature passes Tos (80 °C at power-up) and releases below Thyst (75 °C); both are 9-bit values in 0.5 °C steps in registers 0x03 and 0x02.
The SDA/SCL pull-ups go to VCC, so power the board from 3.3 V on a 3.3 V microcontroller. There is no chip-ID register.

driver.code:
# PCT2075 I2C-bus Fm+ digital temperature sensor and thermal watchdog (NXP PCT2075 Rev. 10.1), MicroPython driver.
# Register pointer: 0x00 Temp (read-only, 2 bytes), 0x01 Conf (1 byte), 0x02 Thyst (2 bytes),
# 0x03 Tos (2 bytes), 0x04 Tidle (1 byte).
# Temp: 11-bit two's complement in bits 15..5, 0.125 degC per LSB; the 5 low bits read as 0.
# Tos/Thyst: 9-bit two's complement in bits 15..7, 0.5 degC per LSB.
import time

_REG_TEMP = 0x00
_REG_CONF = 0x01
_REG_THYST = 0x02
_REG_TOS = 0x03
_REG_TIDLE = 0x04


class PCT2075:
    def __init__(self, i2c, addr=0x37):
        # 0x37 = A0, A1, A2 all floating (Adafruit breakout default); see datasheet Table 5.
        self.i2c = i2c
        self.addr = addr

    def _read16(self, reg):
        d = self.i2c.readfrom_mem(self.addr, reg, 2)
        raw = (d[0] << 8) | d[1]
        return raw - 0x10000 if raw & 0x8000 else raw

    def _write16(self, reg, value):
        value &= 0xFFFF
        self.i2c.writeto_mem(self.addr, reg, bytes([value >> 8, value & 0xFF]))

    def temperature(self):
        """Temperature in degC, 0.125 degC resolution (datasheet section 7.4.3)."""
        return (self._read16(_REG_TEMP) >> 5) * 0.125

    def config(self, value=None):
        """Read (no argument) or write the 8-bit Conf register.
        B4:3 OS fault queue, B2 OS polarity (1 = active high), B1 1 = interrupt mode, B0 1 = shutdown."""
        if value is None:
            return self.i2c.readfrom_mem(self.addr, _REG_CONF, 1)[0]
        self.i2c.writeto_mem(self.addr, _REG_CONF, bytes([value & 0x1F]))

    def shutdown(self, off=True):
        """Conf bit 0: 1 = shutdown (under 1 uA, Temp keeps the last result), 0 = normal."""
        c = self.config()
        self.config((c | 0x01) if off else (c & ~0x01))
        if not off:
            time.sleep_ms(100)  # first new conversion (28 ms) completes within one 100 ms period

    def tos(self, value=None):
        """Overtemperature shutdown threshold in degC (0.5 degC steps, power-up 80)."""
        if value is None:
            return (self._read16(_REG_TOS) >> 7) * 0.5
        self._write16(_REG_TOS, int(round(value * 2)) << 7)

    def thyst(self, value=None):
        """Hysteresis threshold in degC (0.5 degC steps, power-up 75)."""
        if value is None:
            return (self._read16(_REG_THYST) >> 7) * 0.5
        self._write16(_REG_THYST, int(round(value * 2)) << 7)

    def idle_time(self, value=None):
        """Sampling period in 100 ms steps (Tidle[4:0], 1-31; 0 behaves as 1 = 100 ms)."""
        if value is None:
            return self.i2c.readfrom_mem(self.addr, _REG_TIDLE, 1)[0] & 0x1F
        self.i2c.writeto_mem(self.addr, _REG_TIDLE, bytes([value & 0x1F]))

example.code:
from machine import I2C, Pin
import time
from pct2075 import PCT2075

i2c = I2C({I2C_ID}, sda=Pin({SDA}), scl=Pin({SCL}))
sensor = PCT2075(i2c)  # 0x37 with A0, A1, A2 floating
time.sleep_ms(150)  # first conversion is ready within 100 ms of power-up
while True:
    print('T=%.3fC' % sensor.temperature())
    time.sleep(1)
